Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Round End 4 Game Ends Overview Empty your hand the fastest, by playing cards higher than odds, lower than evens, and cards which are the reverse of what the active number is Turn On a turn, you must try to play a card on top of what came before If the current card is odd (+), then you must play a higher card If the current card is even (-), then you must play a lower card If you cannot meet this requirement, then you have to draw a card If you play a card in the 11s, 11, 22, 33, 44 and so on, you get another go straight away If your last played card is the next card you see, i.e. no one else could play, you can play any card ignoring odd or even rules You can interrupt out of turn by playing a mirror of what is displayed, this is the numbers in reverse e.g. 57 can be interrupted with 75, units and whole tens are mirrors of each other e.g. 02 vs 20 If you successfully play a mirror, either discard a card of your choice (not to the play area, out of the game) or cause everyone else to draw a card If you play an invalid card, either normally or the wrong mirror, you take it back and draw a card as penalty Round End The round ends when a player empties their hand Every other player scores 1 point for cards remaining in hand, and 2 points for a card of the 11s in hand Then the cards are shuffled and a new round starts Game Ends Once a player meets or exceeds 25 points, the player with the lowest score wins! Note: At this time, the BGA implementation only plays to 12 points. [Rating: 4/10] This was pretty bad.  The concept is simple, but the execution is boring and frustrating.  At its heart, this is a simple game of playing an available card each turn.  The twist, such as it is, is that you can jump in and play a card that is the reverse of the previously-played card. However, this is not really a strategic choice - there is really no case you would not want to do so -- it is just about whether you are quick enough to do it.  And with that in mind, it all comes down to whether or not you happen to have the right card at the right time, which is not something you can control.  T

[Rating: 5/10] Similar to LLAMA where you're trying to be the first to run out of cards, cards in your hand score points, and the game ends when someone reaches 25 points (winner is lowest score).  There is speed element where you can interrupt the active player if you have the mirror card in your hand (e.g. last card played was 06 and you hold 60).  The scoring seems pretty boring compared to LLAMA - need to try it out more but not sure my group will like it.
